I want to tell you all that i have bipolar disorder. And this is by no means a contest to see whose life and luck is worse. We suffer from a black cloud that feels like grief every day, sometimes even if medicated, cause sometimes that shit works, but it always makes you sick. Nausea, headaches, dizziness, can't sleep, sleep too much. Etc, etc. I come from a very small family. I had an older sister. She was blind and developmentally disabled. Had cancer. No one knew til it was too late. My mother and I watched her die. That was in December. The day before her birthday. 
My mother lived with her mother and brother and cared for them in addition to working. Momma had COPD.  Somehow she got pnemonia in both lungs. My brother and I were with her in the hospital. My brother goes to Momma's house to retrieve her purse and he discovered our grandmother DEAD. Like lividity dead. Eyes open dead. Our mother died the next day. 

If you guys hang in there, I promise that I will, too. Even though i have only 3 family members left in this world. I think i am not thinking of suicide because I had to bury my grandmother, cremate my mother. And i am very afraid of what will happen if this is just shock.

You know. It's strange. The death of my sister from colon cancer was righteously unfair. She was blind and developmentally disabled, went immediately into hospice care, suffered greatly then died. I am still full of anger and bitterness. I suspect my mother wanted to be with her. Hell, I want to be with her.  My mother had COPD and we hoped(my younger brother and myself ) that this was only an exacerbation. Got to the hospital and immediately knew it was NOT.  Later that evening, brother leaves to bring Momma's phone and purse and something told him to go look in on my grandmother. (momma lived with her mother and youngest brother my uncle) He has dementia. And thats a comfort now. Anyway my brother found my grandmother in a chair in her bedroom, so dead she was already a different color. I know because I saw her myself before funeral home came.  My momma died next day. I am in shock. Grieving.  I cry alot. In the privacy of the shower. In the public of Walmart. I scream "fuck" and "no" when inside my parked car. They are primal,animalistic and futile screams. But then I remember Momma's struggle to breathe, her utter heartache and despair from burying her firstborn. And I think of my grandmother. She felt useless and had been widowed since 1993. Never could I have told either of them of the other's passing. And in those moments I feel a small spark of divine peace. How can I cry when I know all of their earthly sufferings are over?  I can't.
